items.front: Where was Magadha located (modern regions)?
items.back: The Patna and Gaya regions of present-day Bihar — the most powerful Mahajanapada.
items.examPoint: Location — Patna & Gaya (Bihar)

items.front: Magadha's two rival neighbours and their fate?
items.back: North: Vajji republic (Licchavis, capital Vaishali). West: Kashi, later conquered by Kosala.
items.examPoint: Neighbours — Vajji republic (Licchavi/Vaishali) & Kashi conquered by Kosala

items.front: Which three rivers formed Magadha's natural defensive ring?
items.back: Ganga, Son and Champa — a natural moat that made invasion difficult.
items.examPoint: Riverine natural defence (Ganga, Son, Champa)

items.front: Magadha's two strategic capital cities?
items.back: Rajgir (Rajagriha) and Pataliputra — both in key military positions in the Gangetic valley.
items.examPoint: Strategic cities — Rajgir & Pataliputra

items.front: Which metals in Magadha's territory enabled advanced weaponry?
items.back: Large copper and iron deposits — the basis of advanced weapons and military technology.
items.examPoint: Copper & iron deposits — advanced weaponry

items.front: Mastery of which river gave Magadha economic dominance?
items.back: The Ganga — crucial for trade in North India.
items.examPoint: Trade routes & mastery over the Ganga

items.front: What did Bimbisara's annexation of Anga give Magadha?
items.back: Control of the Champa River — improving trade with Southeast Asia, Sri Lanka and South India.
items.examPoint: Bimbisara's annexation of Anga & Champa River trade

items.front: Cultural factor that aided Magadha's rise?
items.back: Society not dominated by Brahmanas; many kings of humble origins; Aryan/non-Aryan mix — inclusive and flexible.
items.examPoint: Cultural factors — non-Brahmana society, kings of humble origins, Aryan/non-Aryan mix

items.front: Which animal did Magadhan rulers first use effectively in war?
items.back: Elephants — a decisive tactical advantage, alongside iron weapons and a standing army.
items.examPoint: First effective use of war elephants; iron weapons

items.front: Which two rulers built Magadha's administrative systems?
items.back: Bimbisara and Ajatashatru (Haryanka dynasty) — effective administration over vast territory.
items.examPoint: Rulers Bimbisara & Ajatashatru — administrative systems

items.front: The Vajji confederacy — how many clans, and leading one?
items.back: Eight clans; the Licchavis were the most important, capital Vaishali.
items.examPoint: Neighbours — Vajji republic (Licchavi/Vaishali) & Kashi conquered by Kosala

items.front: When did the struggle that formed the Magadha Empire occur?
items.back: The 6th century BCE — Magadha emerged victorious over Vajji, Kashi and Kosala.
items.examPoint: 6th-century-BCE struggle -> formation of the Magadha Empire

items.front: Magadha's eastern neighbour and its fate?
items.back: Anga, capital Champa — the first state Magadha annexed, under Bimbisara.
items.examPoint: Bimbisara's annexation of Anga & Champa River trade

items.front: Magadha's chief western rival and its king?
items.back: Avanti, under Chanda Pradyota; the Shishunagas finally annexed Avanti.
items.examPoint: Neighbours — Vajji republic (Licchavi/Vaishali) & Kashi conquered by Kosala

items.front: Why is Pataliputra called a jaladurga?
items.back: It was a water fort at the Ganga–Son confluence, protected by rivers on several sides.
items.examPoint: Strategic cities — Rajgir & Pataliputra

items.front: Where were Magadha's richest iron deposits?
items.back: Not far from Rajgir in south Bihar — the source of iron weapons and ploughs.
items.examPoint: Copper & iron deposits — advanced weaponry

items.front: What did Magadha's location give it in trade?
items.back: Control over important trade routes, and the Ganga's North Indian trade.
items.examPoint: Trade routes & mastery over the Ganga

items.front: What kind of rulers did Magadha have?
items.back: Powerful, ambitious rulers who expanded the kingdom through military conquest.
items.examPoint: Political factors — ambitious rulers & strong standing army

items.front: What paid for Magadha's standing army?
items.back: Land revenue — Bhaga, 1/6 of the produce — plus taxes on trade.
items.examPoint: Political factors — ambitious rulers & strong standing army

items.front: Archaeological marker of Magadha's urban economy?
items.back: NBPW (Northern Black Polished Ware) pottery, found with punch-marked coins.
items.examPoint: Trade routes & mastery over the Ganga

items.front: What did Magadha's forests supply?
items.back: Timber for building and elephants for the army.
items.examPoint: First effective use of war elephants; iron weapons

items.front: Bimbisara — dates and royal physician?
items.back: Ruled c. 544–492 BCE; his physician was Jivaka.
items.examPoint: Bimbisara details (Haryanka, Rajagriha/Girivraja, contemporary of Buddha & Mahavira, Jivaka, matrimonial alliances)

items.front: Bimbisara's three marriage alliances?
items.back: Kosaladevi of Kosala (a Kashi village as dowry); Chellana, a Licchavi princess; Kshema of the Madra clan (Punjab).
items.examPoint: Bimbisara details (Haryanka, Rajagriha/Girivraja, contemporary of Buddha & Mahavira, Jivaka, matrimonial alliances)

items.front: Founder of the first non-Kshatriya empire?
items.back: Mahapadma Nanda, founder of the Nanda dynasty.
items.examPoint: Udayin founds Pataliputra; dynastic succession Haryanka -> Shishunaga -> Nanda (Mahapadma/Dhana Nanda, Alexander 326 BCE)

items.front: Bimbisara vs Ajatashatru — how did each expand?
items.back: Bimbisara by marriage alliances and diplomacy (plus Anga); Ajatashatru by war against Kosala and the Vajjis.
items.examPoint: Ajatashatru's conquests & war engines (Rathamusala, Mahashilakantaka); First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha

items.front: Historians who stress iron and surplus in Magadha's rise?
items.back: R. S. Sharma and D. D. Kosambi; H. C. Raychaudhuri stresses dynastic ambition.
items.examPoint: Copper & iron deposits — advanced weaponry
items.source: R. S. Sharma; D. D. Kosambi
